paragraphs.text: 右侧栏 HTML 批注预览：点选元素或框选区域写批注，直接发进当前会话让 AI 改
English · 简体中文
dsh-html-annotate
Point at the part of an HTML page you want changed. Send that pointer to the current session as one
of an HTML page you want changed. Send that pointer to the current session as one ordinary message.
Open a local `.html` file inside a DeepSeek Harness session, preview it in the right sidebar, then c
lick an element, Ctrl/Cmd-click a group, or Shift-drag a region. Whatever you pick lands in the curr
ent session as a normal user message carrying the file path, each element's selector, its text, the
styles it currently has, and the styles you want it to have.
The preview is a real page load from a route on the local Harness server, not a `blob:` document, so
links, `?query` strings and the page's own scripts keep working while you annotate.
No screenshots. No "the card on the right, make it red". The model gets a selector it can grep for.
**Highlights**
- **Click, group, region.** Three ways to point: a single element, up to 24 elements with Ctrl/Cmd-c

lick, or a dragged region sampled into its containing elements.
- **Styles as targets.** Eight field
s — font size, weight, text color, background, corner radius, padding, width, height. Current value

shows as placeholder; fill one in and the message says where it is headed.
- **A preview that still
behaves like a page.** Relative links, query parameters, CDN styles and scripts load natively; the a

nnotation bridge is injected into every HTML response, so it survives navigation inside the frame.
-
**Preview and edit the source.** Use `</>` to open the HTML source, save with the button or `Ctrl/C
md+S`, then return to the rendered page with `▦`. Version checks keep a save from overwriting an ext

ernal edit.
[该节后续省略]
## What gets sent
One element, one style change, one note:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
This is a plain `session.prompt(..., 'queue')` call, so the message shows up in chat history like an
ything you typed, works on any model, and leaves no hidden channel behind.
Current styles are only listed for the keys you actually changed. The seven keys worth diffing are `
font-size`, `font-weight`, `line-height`, `color`, `background-color`, `padding`, `border-radius`; a
nnotated text, ids and class names are filled with noise if the note is about copy or structure.
The `source` line is a best-effort hint: the plugin reads up to 10 local `.js` / `.css` files refere
nced by the entry page (512 KB of code), looks for the element's text, id and class names, and stops
at the first hit. It names the file only — line numbers drift with every edit and a wrong one costs
more than it saves. Inline scripts, files it cannot read, and strings assembled at runtime may not
be found; the hint is simply omitted then, and the message still sends.
## How it works
The plugin is assembled from DSH capability seams rather than reimplementing them:
| DSH capability | How this plugin uses it |
| `webServer.register()` | The Host half registers one `/html-annotate` prefix route for previews, s

ource reads and version-checked saves |
| `sessions` + `connection` | The route maps the session id

in the URL to that session's workspace root, under the same trust gate as DSH's own web routes |
| `
sidebarRightTabs` service + `sidebar.right.pane.tab` slot | Registers the **HTML annotations** tab,

matched only for session-bound `.html` / `.htm` file addresses |
| `remote.workspaceFiles` | The cli
ent reads the entry page once to confirm it is reachable and to keep its source for the `source:` hi

nt; the route serves the bytes |
| Host `fs` service | Resolves workspace paths and writes UTF-8 sou
rce with `replaceIfVersion`, so an external edit produces a conflict instead of being overwritten |
| `remote.changes()` stream | Reloads the preview; falls back to backoff polling when the stream is

unavailable |
| `session.prompt(content, 'queue')` | Delivers the assembled annotation message to th

e session owning the file |
| `locale` service | Registers the `html-annotate` namespace (87 keys pe
r language) and follows live language switches |
Data flow: tab address → `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/html-annotate/s/<session>/<path>` → Host serves th
e page and its assets natively, injecting the bridge into every HTML response → bridge collects sele
ctions → validated and shaped upstream → composed message → queued into the session.
Because the frame is loaded from a URL instead of a `blob:`, the browser resolves the page's own rel
ative links and `location.href = './next.html'` normally, and `?course=...` style parameters survive
tive links and `location.href = './next.html'` normally, and `?course=...` style parameters survive.
Draft state: `idle → picking → occupied → saved → sent`, where *occupied* means the draft already ho
lds a note or style targets. A saved annotation can be reopened by clicking its element again, and e
diting replaces it in place.
## Known limitations
- The frame is sandboxed without `allow-same-origin`, so `sessionStorage` / `localStorage` throw ins
ide it. Pages that persist state there degrade to in-memory; pages that read them without a `try/cat

ch` lose that handler.
- Only files under the session's workspace root are served. Absolute-path add
resses (`absolute/...`) keep going to the built-in preview, which is a static snapshot and does not

run page scripts the same way.
- The page's own remote references load natively — CDN styles, script
s and images included. That is the point of a real preview, and it also means the preview makes netw

ork requests the Harness does not mediate.
- Navigation inside the frame stays inside the plugin: fo
llowing a link to an external site loads that site without the annotation bridge, so annotation stop

s working there.
- The change stream is best effort; when it is unavailable the preview falls back t

o polling with exponential backoff up to 20 seconds.
- Source editing supports UTF-8 HTML. UTF-16 an

d GB18030 files stay read-only because saving decoded text could change their encoding.
- An externa
l file change does not replace an unsaved source draft. Re-read or save after reviewing the conflict

; saving with an old version is rejected.
- No screenshots are taken. What the model sees is structu
re, text and computed styles.
## Compatibility

| DSH | `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0` (`engines.dsh`) |
| Surface | Web GUI right sidebar (`dsh.client.platfo

rm: "web"`); headless and TUI profiles have no sidebar |
| Node | `>=20`, tests only |
